evidence: completion-gate.ts findReviewGateState and sessionReviewRoots.

quote: for (const match of text.matchAll(REVIEW_PACKAGE_PATH)) {
problem: sessionReviewRoots runs REVIEW_PACKAGE_PATH over every history message and every tool-call argument. The pattern starts with a lazy run of non-delimiter characters before the literal `.metaproject`, so at each start index it expands to the end of the current delimiter-free token. A token of length L with no `.metaproject/reviews` in it costs O(L^2). agent.ts now calls it from holdReviewGate on every stop attempt once a review run is seen.
impact: A tool result holding one long delimiter-free token (base64 image or blob, long hash list, minified text with no quotes, whitespace, parens or semicolons) of about 100 KB costs billions of regex steps, a multi-second synchronous stall of the shell event loop on every stop attempt; 1 MB is minutes. Failure mode: the shell freezes at the point the review gate is meant to nudge, repeated per stop attempt because nothing is cached.
suggested_fix: Do not scan with a lazy-prefix regex. Find each `.metaproject/reviews/` with indexOf and walk backwards over the allowed prefix characters (bounded, e.g. 512 chars). Skip messages without the substring. Optionally cache roots per history length so a stop attempt scans only new messages.
evidence: src/review/completion-gate.ts REVIEW_PACKAGE_PATH is a regex with a lazy `[^\s"'`<>|;&()]*?` prefix before `\.metaproject`; scan() is applied to message.content and call.arguments for the whole history; called at src/commands/agent.ts holdReviewGate (diff hunk @@ 3467,3507 @@). Not executed; derived from the pattern.

class_scope.enumeration_method: keryx ctx rg for sessionReviewRoots and REVIEW_PACKAGE_PATH in src (non-test): one definition, one use inside scan(), one caller

quote: const scanned = await scanRoot(root, since);
problem: The extra roots come from every path in the session transcript that matches `.metaproject/reviews/`, with no cap. findReviewGateState scans each one in sequence (readdir plus a JSON.parse of every package manifest.json, plus resolveActiveReview), on every stop attempt, with no caching.
impact: A tool result listing many projects (a find over a workspace of several hundred checkouts) turns each stop attempt into hundreds of sequential directory scans and file reads, a seconds-long stall at 100s of roots. Bounded by transcript content, not by request rate.
suggested_fix: Cap extraRoots (e.g. the 8 most recently named), or restrict to roots that hold a manifest younger than `since`; cache the scan per (root, history length).
evidence: sessionReviewRoots returns [...roots] unbounded; findReviewGateState loops over roots calling scanRoot for each.

quote: "treat the task as not done and re-dispatch it.",
problem: The new empty-reply error tells the parent to re-dispatch with no bound or backoff, and the path writes no KERYX_USAGE line (it returns before saveChildResult), so the tokens burned by each empty child are recorded as unknown.
impact: Failure mode: a model that is persistently empty (context overflow, refusing provider) in a wave of N children is re-dispatched each time, each costing a full prompt; at wave scale spend grows N x retries and the ledger's token spend reads as a lower bound that hides it. The round ceiling and wave budget still bound it, hence minor.
suggested_fix: State a retry cap in the message (or rely on a named cap) and, when childUsage.known, still record the usage (append to the save target or put it in the Error output) so failed dispatches count toward spend.
evidence: The empty-reply branch returns Error before the saveNote/saveChildResult line that appends usageSuffix().

quote: if (status === "Completed" && raw === "(subagent produced no text)" && turnResult?.submittedResult === undefined) {
problem: Emptiness is detected by comparing against the placeholder string literal, which is duplicated in the raw computation and in the hadText check; rewording one of the three sites silently disables or misfires the guard.
impact: Failure mode: if the placeholder is reworded in one place, empty children return to being reported Completed and the parent treats a no-result reviewer as success on every wave (the defect flow 460 E removes).
suggested_fix: Compute a boolean (const producedNoText = ...) once where raw is built and use it at all three sites.
evidence: Three occurrences of the literal in this file (raw computation, hadText, new guard).

quote: const REVIEW_PACKAGE_PATH = /((?:[A-Za-z]:)?[^\s"'`<>|;&()]*?)\.metaproject[\\/]reviews[\\/]([^\\/\s"'`<>|;&()]+)/g;
title: Quadratic regex scan over every message and tool result on each gate evaluation
problem: The lazy prefix group [^\s"'`<>|;&()]*? is tried from every start offset and, for a run of n non-delimiter characters containing no '.metaproject', scans to the end of the run each time: O(n^2) per run. sessionReviewRoots applies it to every history message content and every tool-call argument string, synchronously, on each gate evaluation (up to MAX_REVIEW_GATE_CONTINUES = 20 per run).
impact: Failure mode: a tool result holding one unbroken token (base64 blob, minified single line with no spaces/quotes/parens, long hash list) of ~1 MB costs ~5e11 steps and freezes the shell event loop for minutes at the first gate check after it; ~100 KB costs several seconds per gate turn. It repeats every turn because the whole history is rescanned.
suggested_fix: Cheap pre-check: skip any text where !text.includes('.metaproject'). Then drop the lazy prefix: match /\.metaproject[\\/]reviews[\\/]([^\\/\s"'`<>|;&()]+)/g and recover the prefix by walking backwards from match.index over the delimiter class (linear). Also scan only messages added since the previous gate call.
evidence: regex literal at the REVIEW_PACKAGE_PATH declaration; scan() iterates text.matchAll for each history message and each toolCall.arguments in sessionReviewRoots

class_scope.enumeration_method: read the full slice diff; the only new regex over unbounded session text is REVIEW_PACKAGE_PATH, consumed in one scan() closure

quote: const roots = [cwd, ...extraRoots.filter((r) => path.resolve(r) !== path.resolve(cwd))];
title: Session-named roots are unbounded and each is rescanned (readdir, manifest reads, signature hash) every gate turn
problem: sessionReviewRoots returns every distinct directory any tool output named through a '.metaproject/reviews/' path, with no cap and no check that the root exists or is a project. findReviewGateState then runs scanRoot (readdir plus a manifest read and stat per package) and resolveActiveReview for each, and findReviewGateState is evaluated again on every continue.
impact: Failure mode: a session that greps or reads docs/logs naming many distinct review paths (e.g. a multi-repo listing, dozens to hundreds of roots) multiplies per-turn filesystem work by the root count, for up to 20 continues. Linear, not catastrophic; it also makes gate latency depend on transcript content.
suggested_fix: Cap the roots (e.g. most recent 8), drop roots with no .metaproject directory before the loop, and memoise the set across turns by history length.
evidence: sessionReviewRoots builds an unbounded Set; findReviewGateState loops all roots

quote: const coverage = problems.length === 0 ? await packageCoverageErrors(ctx.dir, dispatch) : [];
title: Readiness now runs the full coverage gate, including a 15 s git diff, on every evaluation
problem: reviewersCheck used to read files only. It now calls packageCoverageErrors, which for a dispatch that says depth light goes through packageDiffStats and spawns git rev-parse plus git diff -U20 (15 s timeout, 8 MB buffer) and several package reads, on each computeReadiness call. computeReadiness is called from review.ts, operator-confirm-review.ts, the TUI readiness panel and status paths.
impact: Failure mode: a status/panel refresh loop or repeated 'review readiness' on a large light-depth PR spawns a diff process per refresh (up to 15 s each, serial), so the panel stalls on large diffs. Bounded by the timeout; not a crash.
suggested_fix: Memoise the coverage verdict per (package head, manifest mtime, dispatch hash), or run the git-backed light-depth check only from 'review complete' and have readiness report the cached result.
evidence: reviewersCheck awaits packageCoverageErrors unconditionally when the dispatch is valid

quote: const USAGE_LINE = /^[ \t]*KERYX_USAGE[ \t]+(\{[^\n]*\})[ \t]*\r?$/gm;
title: Backtracking on a long KERYX_USAGE line with many closing braces
problem: For a line that starts with KERYX_USAGE, '\{[^\n]*\}' is greedy then backtracks to each earlier '}' while '[ \t]*\r?$' keeps failing, so a line with k '}' characters and a non-matching tail costs O(k * line length). Reviewer replies are model/attacker-influenced text; splitUsage runs on every parse and emptiness check of a raw result.
impact: Failure mode: a single 1 MB line of '}' after the marker costs ~1e12 steps on the ingest path. Needs the marker at line start with a bad tail, so it is unlikely by accident.
suggested_fix: Match the line with [^\n]* only, then validate by trimming and checking the last char is '}' and JSON.parse inside the try block; or cap the line length (e.g. 4 KB) before applying the regex.
evidence: USAGE_LINE definition; used in splitUsage via matchAll and replace

quote: reads the package and prints eleven items, READY or NOT READY

quote: `review ingest` keeps an internal finding whose `quote` is not at its `path` at the reviewed SHA
problem: The rewritten rule replaces "refuses" with "keeps ... instead of refusing the round" but drops the cases that still refuse. `refuseUnresolvedLocators` (src/review/managed.ts:1478-1505) still throws `Cannot ingest review` for an internal finding whose quote could not be checked at all: the head commit is not in the checkout, the finding quotes code but names no file, or a size bound stopped the match.

suggested_fix: Append the remaining refusal: "It still refuses a quote it could not check at all (the commit is not in this checkout, no file named, or a size bound stopped the match); re-quote or dismiss that finding with evidence."

quote: const partialSaved = saveTarget.abs === undefined || partial.length === 0 ? undefined : await saveTimedOutPartial(saveTarget.abs, `${partial}${usageSuffix()}`);
problem: The usage line is written only where a file is saved, and only with what has been reported by then. (a) Timeout: `usageSuffix()` is evaluated when the deadline fires, before the in-flight request has emitted its `usage_update`, so the line understates that dispatch but is written as an ordinary known count. A timed-out child with no text writes no file at all. (b) The new empty-reply branch returns with no `saveChildResult` call, so the tokens that child spent are never recorded. `usageTotals` (src/review/ledger.ts:631) counts dispatches from the raw files, so an empty-reply dispatch is not counted as a dispatch and the totals can report `complete: true` ("token spend: X over N dispatch(es)") while omitting it.
impact: The review's stated spend, which the flow adds so cost can be stated (H), is silently low on the two failure paths most likely to burn tokens (timeouts, empty replies that are then re-dispatched), and it is labelled complete rather than a lower bound.
suggested_fix: On the empty-reply path, when save_result_to is set and usage is known, write the usage line (or a usage-only sidecar the ledger counts as a dispatch with an empty body). On the timeout path, mark the line as partial (for example `"partial":true`) and have usageTotals treat a partial dispatch as making the totals a lower bound.
evidence: spawn-subagent-tool.ts timeout branch (head ~2244) and the empty-reply branch (~2316-2335) that returns before the save at ~2363; dispatch-usage.ts usageTotals sets complete when every counted usage is known; ledger.ts:631 builds totals from raws.

quote: new RegExp(`\b${MANDATORY_INPUT}\b[^.\n]{0,80}${UNREADABLE}`, "i"),
problem: The flow 460 D check that marks a DONE reply as incomplete when it says it could not read a mandatory input matches ordinary finding summaries. The second pattern only needs the word `schema`, `payload`, `context file` and so on, followed within 80 characters by `missing`, `not found`, `is not`, `does not exist` and similar. It does not require a reading verb or a first-person subject. So the summary `reviewer-finding.schema.json is missing a slices property` matches: the \b before `schema` holds after the dot. So does `the payload parser is missing a guard for empty slices`, and so does `the schema is unchanged and nothing is missing`. Each one moves a finished reviewer to status incomplete with scopeComplete false.
impact: If a reviewer reports a real defect about a schema or a payload, and this repository's review code is built from both, the ledger records that reviewer as not having finished. The gap reads `the reply states a mandatory input could not be read`, scopeReviewed goes false and `keryx review complete` refuses. The operator then re-dispatches a reviewer that did finish. That is the readiness/complete disagreement loop flow 460 was written to remove. The new tests at src/review/ledger.test.ts (`D: a DONE reply that states a mandatory input could not be read is incomplete`) check three positive phrasings and one benign summary that never puts an input noun before a negation word, so they do not catch this.
suggested_fix: Anchor the claim to the reviewer's own reading. Require a first-person or passive reading verb next to the input noun in both patterns: drop the bare `missing` and `is/are not` alternatives from the noun-first form, or require `(?:could not|couldn't|cannot|unable to|failed to) (?:read|open|load|access|find)` in both orders. Add negative cases to ledger.test.ts, such as `reviewer-finding.schema.json is missing a slices property` and `the payload parser is missing a guard`, and assert that they stay complete.
evidence: Read src/review/ledger.ts:19-31 and 505-536. UNREADABLE includes `missing`, `not\s+found` and `(?:is|are)(?:\s+not)`. Pattern 2 is `\b<input>\b[^.\n]{0,80}<UNREADABLE>`. MANDATORY_INPUT includes the bare `schema` and `payload`. A non-undefined claim forces `finished` to false at line 506.

class_scope.enumeration_method: keryx ctx rg 'unreadableInputClaim|UNREADABLE_INPUT' src: the only producer is ledger.ts:21-31 and the only consumer is ledger.ts:505. Both patterns in UNREADABLE_INPUT share the over-broad UNREADABLE alternation; pattern 2 (line 23) is the one with no verb requirement.

quote: new RegExp(`\\b${MANDATORY_INPUT}\\b[^.\\n]{0,80}${UNREADABLE}`, "i"),
problem: unreadableInputClaim treats any summary in which one of the MANDATORY_INPUT words (payload, schema, review schema, result schema, pr context, context file, slice manifest) is followed within 80 non-period characters by any UNREADABLE alternative as a claim that the reviewer could not read its inputs. UNREADABLE includes the bare negations `is not`, `are not`, `was not`, `can't` and the word `missing`, and the second regex needs no read/open/load verb. Ordinary defect prose matches it. Examples: 'the dispatch payload is missing slices', 'the finding schema is not updated for usage', 'pr-context is not passed to the light check'. In keryx's own review code, which is mostly about payloads, schemas and PR context, this kind of sentence is routine.
impact: When it matches, the reviewer's DONE result is recorded as `incomplete`, scopeComplete false, and a gap tells the operator to run retry-plan. Re-dispatching the same scope gets a similar summary and the same rejection. The round cannot reach scopeReviewed until someone rewords the reviewer's prose, so a finished review stays open.
suggested_fix: Require an explicit inability phrase tied to a read verb in both patterns, for example `(could not|cannot|unable to|failed to) (read|open|load|access|find|parse) ... <input>` and `<input> ... (not found|does not exist|no such file|permission denied|unreadable)`. Drop the bare `is not` / `are not` / `was not` / `missing` alternatives, or anchor them to a read verb. Add negative tests built from ordinary defect summaries that mention payload, schema and PR context.
evidence: ledger.ts:20 defines UNREADABLE with `(?:could|can|did|was|were|is|are)(?:\s+not|n['’]t)` and `missing`. ledger.ts:23 builds the second pattern as MANDATORY_INPUT, then [^.\n]{0,80}, then UNREADABLE. ledger.ts (buildLedger) sets `finished = FINISHED.has(status) && asked.length === 0 && unreadable === undefined` and sends unfinished runs to the retry gap. Example: summary 'The payload is missing the layers block' gives regex 2 a match on 'payload is missing'.

class_scope.enumeration_method: keryx ctx rg 'UNREADABLE_INPUT|unreadableInputClaim' src/review: two patterns built from the one UNREADABLE alternation, and one consumer (buildLedger's `finished`)

quote: if (pointer === undefined || Date.parse(pointer.startedAt) < since) continue;
problem: findReviewGateState now ignores an open package whose manifest is older than the session's first message (`if (info.mtimeMs < since) continue;`). It also ignores an active-review pointer whose startedAt is older. A shell session that resumes a review opened in an earlier session matches both conditions until something rewrites the manifest. Reading the package (`review status`, `review readiness`, dispatching reviewers) does not rewrite it. In that window the gate returns the placeholder 'no review package exists: `keryx review start` has not opened one', and nextStep tells the model to run `keryx review start --pr <n>`.
impact: A resumed review is nudged to open a second package for the same PR instead of finishing the one the pointer names. The flow-460 description asked for the session start to be honoured, but the pointer exists to name the run in progress, and here its age vetoes it.
suggested_fix: Honour a live pointer whatever its startedAt when this session's history names its package dir or review id (sessionReviewRoots already scans the history). Alternatively, keep the since-filter for scanned candidates only and not for the pointer.
evidence: completion-gate.ts:93 `if (info.mtimeMs < since) continue;` and :126 pointer age check. sessionStartedAt is the first message ts. nextStep, for packageDir === '', prints the `keryx review start` instruction.

quote: const REVIEW_PACKAGE_PATH = /((?:[A-Za-z]:)?[^\s"'`<>|;&()]*?)\.metaproject[\\/]reviews[\\/]([^\\/\s"'`<>|;&()]+)/g;
problem: sessionReviewRoots adds a root for every `.metaproject/reviews/<x>` path found in any message content, tool results included, not only in the session's own commands. The pointer loop then takes the first root whose pointer is fresh. When cwd has no fresh pointer, for example before this session ran `review start`, a pointer in another worktree or checkout wins. That only needs some tool output in the history to quote that root's package path while a concurrent session there has started a review after this session began. The prefix also absorbs flag syntax such as `--package=out/x/`, which yields a bogus root (harmless, since readdir fails).
impact: Within the narrow window it describes, the gate can again nudge about another session's review, which is the defect C this flow set out to close.
suggested_fix: Collect roots only from the session's own tool-call arguments and from the output of `keryx review start|attach`, not from arbitrary tool results. Or prefer the root whose pointer's package dir appears verbatim in the history.
evidence: completion-gate.ts:62-71 scans `message.content` (tool results) as well as toolCalls arguments. completion-gate.ts:124-131 takes the first fresh pointer across all roots.

quote: const recordedBase = str(target.base);
problem: packageDiffStats documents that the light recheck diffs 'against the recorded `target.base`', but `keryx review start|ingest` never records one. runCreate builds `target: { kind, ref, head }`, and `--base` is passed only to findPreviousRound (review.ts:1093). Only the bot runner writes target.base. For CLI-started packages recordedBase is always undefined, so a PR whose base is not main/master is diffed against origin/main.
impact: For a PR into a long-lived branch such as develop or a stacked PR, `origin/main...head` includes every commit on that branch. A genuinely small PR is then refused its light round, and defect A remains for those targets. This fails safe (full set), so it is minor.
suggested_fix: Persist `--base` into manifest.target.base in runCreate (and in review plan's handoff), so the documented base order holds for CLI packages.
evidence: src/commands/review.ts:1045 `target: { kind: targetKind, ref: targetRef, ...(head === undefined ? {} : { head }) }`. git grep finds no writer of target.base outside src/review/bot/run.ts:339.

quote: base = (await resolveBase(defaultGitRunner(cwd), { kind, ref: ref ?? "", base: recordedBase }, head))?.ref;
problem: When every base candidate gives an empty range, resolveBase returns that empty-range base rather than null. This is the case of a merged PR with no recorded base. packageDiffStats does not check for it, so the diff is empty: files [] and changedLines 0. autoDepth then returns light for 0 files, and a dispatch that says light is accepted on the strength of an empty range.
impact: In that case the coverage gate accepts the smaller light reviewer set without having seen the PR's real size. review plan warns loudly on the same range (emptyRangeWarning), but the gate stays silent.
suggested_fix: Treat an empty range as unresolved here: call emptyRangeWarning(base, head) and return `{ error }` with that text, so the full set applies until a base is given.
evidence: prior-round.ts:320-330 returns `empty` when every candidate's merge-base equals the head. coverage.ts autoDepth returns light when files.length 0 and changedLines 0 pass every gate.

quote: if (status === "complete") entries.push({ reviewer, status: "run", reason: "dispatched; the research ledger records it complete" });
problem: coverageFromResearch lists every `status: complete` run as 'dispatched'. That includes the runs buildLedger synthesises for roles that slice routing gave no slice (`routedOut: true`, rawEvidence pointing at manifest#roles). Those reviewers were never dispatched and returned no result.
impact: coverage.md, which readiness item 6 holds to 'states the ingest status of each reviewer truthfully', says a routed-out reviewer was dispatched and ran. Readers of the package then see more reviewers run than actually did.
suggested_fix: Check `routedOut === true` and record it as `status: run` with reason 'routed out: slice routing gave this role no slice' (or a separate status), not 'dispatched'.
evidence: ledger.ts buildLedger pushes `{ status: "complete", routedOut: true, ... }` for routedOut roles. coverageFromResearch reads only reviewer/status/notRunReason/executionReason.

quote: return reviewers.length === 1 && reviewers[0] ? reviewers[0] : "review-orchestrator";
problem: Without --reviewers, the `reviewers` list given to normalizeFindings is now the complete runs from research.json, where it was the stand-in ['review-orchestrator']. If exactly one run is complete, defaultReviewer and legacyReviewer attribute every report finding that names no reviewer to that one reviewer. Example: one reviewer finished and the others are incomplete or not-run, and the orchestrator's report.md is parsed by the legacy reader.

suggested_fix: Keep the attribution default separate from coverage. Pass ['review-orchestrator'] (or input.reviewers) as the attribution fallback and use coverageFromResearch only for coverage.md.

quote: if (omitted.length > 0) return bad(`coverage.md omits ${some(omitted)}, which the dispatch record ran`, `re-run keryx review ingest <input> for this package: it writes coverage.md from the dispatch record`);
problem: The new omitted-reviewer check fails item 6 whenever coverage.md does not list every run in the dispatch record, including routed-out and not-run entries. The repair it prints is wrong for one path. normalizeCoverage uses an explicit `--reviewers` list ahead of the research record, so re-running ingest with the same `--reviewers a,b` writes the same coverage.md and the item fails again. Packages ingested before this change with the review-orchestrator stand-in also fail, with the same advice.

suggested_fix: Name the cause in the repair ('re-run ingest without --reviewers so coverage.md is written from research.json'), or let normalizeCoverage merge the research runs into an explicit --reviewers list.

quote: const REVIEW_PACKAGE_PATH = /((?:[A-Za-z]:)?[^\s"'`<>|;&()]*?)\.metaproject[\\/]reviews[\\/]([^\\/\s"'`<>|;&()]+)/g;
problem: REVIEW_PACKAGE_PATH has no literal prefix and begins with a lazy `[^\s"'`<>|;&()]*?` that must extend to the end of the current run of path-safe characters before the `.metaproject` literal can fail. matchAll tries every start offset, so one run of k such characters costs O(k^2). sessionReviewRoots feeds it every string message content and every tool-call arguments string of the whole session history.
impact: Hot path: findReviewGateState runs on every turn end of a managed review run (up to MAX_REVIEW_GATE_CONTINUES = 20 evaluations), each time over the entire, growing history. Reproducible input: a tool result that holds one long run with no whitespace, quote, bracket, pipe, semicolon or ampersand, for example a base64 or hex dump, a lockfile integrity blob or a minified one-line asset read during the review. A 200 KB run is about 2e10 regex steps, a multi-second to minute stall of the shell's event loop at the gate, repeated on each continue. Ordinary prose and JSON (which contains quotes) stay linear, so this is input dependent, not constant.
suggested_fix: Anchor the scan on the literal first: find each `.metaproject/reviews/` (or `.metaproject\\reviews\\`) occurrence with indexOf/a literal-prefixed regex, then walk backwards a bounded number of characters (or to the previous delimiter) to recover the prefix. Alternatively cap the scanned length per message (for example the first and last 64 KB). Also cache the roots found so far and scan only messages added since the last evaluation.

class_scope.enumeration_method: read slice-04 for regex literals applied to unbounded transcript or reply text; the other new unbounded-text regexes (USAGE_LINE, UNREADABLE_INPUT) are bounded or linear and are reported separately as info

evidence: diff of slice-04, src/review/completion-gate.ts: see quote

quote: if (typeof message.content === "string") scan(message.content);
problem: sessionReviewRoots is a pure function of the whole history and is recomputed from scratch on every gate evaluation; nothing remembers which messages were already scanned. Each result root then costs an extra readdir plus a read and stat of every manifest.json under that root's reviews dir (scanRoot) and a resolveActiveReview.
impact: Per gate evaluation (at most 20 per run) the cost grows with total transcript size, which includes large tool results. Correct, but it is work proportional to history that an incremental scan (index of last scanned message) would make proportional to the new messages only.
suggested_fix: Keep a per-session cursor (last scanned index) and a Set of roots in the gate's state, and scan only messages after the cursor.
evidence: diff lines for sessionReviewRoots: loops `for (const message of history)` with no cursor; findReviewGateState passes the result as extraRoots each call.

quote: const coverage = problems.length === 0 ? await packageCoverageErrors(ctx.dir, dispatch) : [];
problem: reviewersCheck now runs the complete coverage gate (packageScopeFiles, packageChangedLines, blast-radius and PR-context probes, pendingMutants, and, for a dispatch that says depth light, effectiveDepth -> packageDiffStats) on every readiness computation. packageDiffStats spawns git rev-parse --show-toplevel (up to twice, sequentially), up to five git rev-parse calls in resolveBase, and a git diff -U20 over the whole PR scope with a 15 s timeout and an 8 MB buffer.
impact: Readiness is read by `review status`, the panel and `review complete` (complete already runs the same gate through packageResearchErrors), so a light-depth package pays for the same git diff at least twice per close and once per status or panel refresh. Only light-depth dispatches reach the git path, and only on a big PR does -U20 get costly, so this is a repeated cost, not a hang.
suggested_fix: Memoise the packageDiffStats result per (packageDir, manifest head) for the lifetime of one command, or let complete pass its already computed coverage errors into computeReadiness. Use `git diff --numstat`/`--name-only` instead of -U20 if only the file list and line count are needed.
evidence: diff of readiness.ts reviewersCheck and research.ts packageCoverageErrors, plus coverage.ts packageDiffStats git spawns.

quote: const cwd = (await gitTopLevel(options.packageDir)) ?? (await gitTopLevel(options.root));
problem: Every packageDiffStats call starts one or two sequential git processes just to find the repository top level, before the base is resolved (up to five more rev-parse spawns inside resolveBase, run one after another) and the diff itself. The top level of a package directory does not change within a command, and the base candidates are independent probes.
impact: Up to roughly eight process spawns of latency before the diff, per light-depth coverage check. Small per call; it multiplies with PERF-003.
suggested_fix: Cache gitTopLevel by directory for the process, and probe the base candidates in parallel or with a single `git rev-parse --verify` over all names.
evidence: gitTopLevel is awaited inline; resolveBase is imported dynamically and run per call.

quote: "treat the task as not done and re-dispatch it.",

A write-mode child (shell.ts / tui-shell.ts parents) can call tools that edit files and never emit assistant text. raw then falls back to '(subagent produced no text)' because history holds no assistant content. Outcome: the parent is told the task was not done and to re-dispatch it, so edits or commands the child already applied can run a second time. The PR intent (D/E) is about an empty reviewer child counting as coverage, and it does not discuss write-mode children.

quote: const claimed = result.slices === undefined ? assigned.ids : readSliceIds(result.slices).ids.filter((id) => allowed.has(id));
problem: Flow 460 D changed src/review/ledger.ts buildLedger so that a reply with no `slices` claims no slice (`const ids = sliceIdsOf(reply.slices);`, with the `closed ? assigned` branch removed). The sibling reader in src/review/retry-eval.ts collectLateResults was not changed. It still credits a DONE or DONE_WITH_CONCERNS reply that has no `slices` with the driver's whole assignment, and its comment still says this is the ledger's rule ("Same rule as the ledger ... no list means the whole assignment"). The two readers now disagree, and the stale one feeds the new one. evaluateRetry passes `late.covered` into planRetry as `covered`, planRetry writes it to `state.reviewers[reviewer].covered`, and `review next --apply` (review-next.ts:154) or `retry-plan` saves it to slices/retry-state.json. ledger.ts buildLedger then adds every `known?.covered` id to `claimed` (`for (const id of known?.covered ?? Outcome: retry-state records every assigned slice as covered, the ledger sees scopeComplete: true, and coverage is claimed for slices the reviewer never named. This is the false coverage flow 460 D was meant to stop. Without --apply, `review next` reports done (no dispatch owed) while `ledger build` reports the uncovered slices as a gap, so the two commands give the operator opposite answers.

quote: ? await findReviewGateState(process.cwd(), sessionStartedAt(history), sessionReviewRoots(history, process.cwd())).catch(() => null)
problem: The change to src/review/completion-gate.ts findReviewGateState/scanRoot now skips every open package whose manifest.json mtime is before `since` (`if (info.mtimeMs < since) continue;`), where before only stale `ingest`-mode drafts were skipped. The gate then returns the placeholder `(no package yet)` with the blocker "no review package exists: `keryx review start` has not opened one", and nextStep tells the model to run `keryx review start`.

In that turn it dispatches reviewers and saves raw results but writes nothing that touches manifest.json. Outcome: the stop gate states something false (that no package exists) and pushes the model, for up to 20 continues, to open a second package for the same PR instead of finishing the one the active pointer names. Before this change the gate named the open package.

quote: ? await findReviewGateState(process.cwd(), sessionStartedAt(history), sessionReviewRoots(history, process.cwd())).catch(() => null)
problem: The review-gate now derives extra project roots from every string in the session history, including role:"tool" messages whose content is raw tool output (file reads, diffs, fetched pages, child replies; agent.ts pushes `content: withBudgetWarning(result.output)` / `scrubControlNonce(output, nonce)` into history). sessionReviewRoots matches any `<prefix>.metaproject/reviews/<x>` substring with REVIEW_PACKAGE_PATH and resolves the prefix against cwd with no containment check. findReviewGateState then (a) honours an active-review pointer found under any of those roots (resolveActiveReview only checks the pointer's dir is inside that same root, and `startedAt` is a self-declared string compared with `since`), (b) otherwise takes the newest open manifest across all roots, and (c) returns null (gate accepts the stop) when any root holds a `status: closed` review manifest with mtime >= session start newer than the chosen package. The chosen manifest's `reviewId` is interpolated into the nudge, which is pushed as a `role: "user"`, `provenance: "harness"` message.
impact: Attack vector: the shell reviews an untrusted PR (or reads any untrusted file/page). The PR adds e.g. `fixtures/x/.metaproject/reviews/r1/manifest.json` with `mode: review-flow` and either (1) `status: closed` — once checked out during the session its mtime is >= since, so when the model's tool output mentions that path the gate returns null and the model may stop with the real review incomplete (completion-gate bypass), or (2) open with `reviewId` set to instruction text plus `fixtures/x/.metaproject/data/review-active/active-review.json` with a future `startedAt` — when cwd has no pointer (the subdirectory-package case this flow targets), that pointer wins and the attacker string is delivered to the model inside a harness-provenance nudge, i.e. untrusted content is promoted to the harness's trusted channel. Preconditions not established by the diff: the PR must carry the crafted files, the path must surface in a tool result, and (for 2) cwd must lack its own live pointer — hence major, not blocker. Before this change only cwd was scanned.
suggested_fix: Derive extra roots only from trusted sources: the stdout of keryx's own `review start`/`review plan` tool calls (or the arguments of `keryx review` commands the model issued), not from arbitrary tool-result or user content; require each root to be inside the repository/cwd tree and to hold a package whose manifest was written by this process (e.g. match the caller token `review start` recorded in the pointer against the session's token). Do not let an extra root's closed manifest short-circuit the gate (`closedAt` only from cwd or from the package this session started), and render `reviewId` through a strict id pattern (e.g. /^[A-Za-z0-9._-]{1,120}$/, else the directory name) before it enters a harness nudge.

quote: const { usage } = splitUsage(body);
problem: The usage channel trusts any `KERYX_USAGE {...}` line in the raw result file. dispatch-usage.ts states the line wins over a result's `usage` "because the host measured it and the reviewer cannot", but on Claude Code and Codex the reviewer writes `<package>/raw/<reviewer>.txt` itself (review-orchestrator SKILL.md Hosts table) and the orchestrator only appends a line when its spawn tool reported tokens. A reviewer (or a diff that prompt-injects it) can emit its own KERYX_USAGE line; with no host line appended after it, that value is recorded as measured. Counts are also unbounded (any finite non-negative number is accepted).
impact: Attack vector: injected text in a reviewed diff makes a reviewer end its reply with `KERYX_USAGE {"tokens_in":0,"tokens_out":0}` (or 1e15); ledger build records it per run and research.json/report.md state a falsified token spend that looks host-measured. Integrity of a reporting metric only; no gate decision reads it.
suggested_fix: Record provenance with the usage (e.g. `source: host|reviewer`) and accept the line as host-measured only when keryx shell's spawn_subagent wrote it (e.g. a host-only marker or a separate `raw/<reviewer>.usage.json` written by the host, never inside the reviewer-authored body); cap counts at a sane maximum; correct the comment's claim that the reviewer cannot write the line.

quote: const REVIEW_PACKAGE_PATH = /((?:[A-Za-z]:)?[^\s"'`<>|;&()]*?)\.metaproject[\\/]reviews[\\/]([^\\/\s"'`<>|;&()]+)/g;
problem: sessionReviewRoots runs REVIEW_PACKAGE_PATH with matchAll over the content of every history message and every tool-call argument. The pattern opens with an unanchored lazy class `[^\s"'`<>|;&()]*?` that must be followed by the literal `.metaproject`. On a run of L characters with no whitespace/quote/delimiter and no `.metaproject`, every start position scans forward to the end of the run before failing, so one scan costs O(L^2). Attack vector: the author of the PR under review adds a long unbroken token (a minified bundle, a base64 fixture, a single-line JSON/SVG with no spaces or quotes, a long URL) to a file in the PR; the reviewing agent reads the diff or the file, the tool result is pushed into `history`, and from then on holdReviewGate (src/commands/agent.ts:3487) calls sessionReviewRoots(history, process.cwd()) on every turn end of a session that has run `keryx review ...`. A 100 KB token is ~5e9 regex steps, a 1 MB token ~5e11, repeated at each stop and up to MAX_REVIEW_GATE_CONTINUES times.
impact: The interactive keryx shell stalls (CPU-bound, synchronous regex on the main loop) at every stop of a review session whose transcript holds such a token, i.e. a denial of service triggered by content of the PR being reviewed. Major rather than blocker: whether a token that long reaches history unbroken depends on tool-result size limits this diff does not establish; the quadratic shape itself is in the code.
suggested_fix: Do not scan with an unbounded lazy prefix. Find each occurrence with indexOf('.metaproject/reviews/') (and the backslash form), then walk backwards to the nearest delimiter to recover the prefix, which is linear. Alternatively cap the prefix (`{0,1024}?`) and skip messages longer than a fixed bound, or scan only toolCalls arguments and the outputs of `keryx review start|attach` instead of all message content. Add a test with a 1 MB unbroken token asserting the scan finishes under a time bound.
evidence: src/review/completion-gate.ts:43 (pattern), :61-64 (scan over every message.content and call.arguments), src/commands/agent.ts:3487 (called on each stop when reviewRunSeenInHistory is true). Complexity follows from the pattern: the only fixed text is after the lazy class, so a failing start position consumes the whole delimiter-free run. Not measured here (read-only review); a one-line bun timing of matchAll over 'a'.repeat(200000) would settle the magnitude.

quote: if (typeof message.content === "string") scan(message.content);
problem: Extra gate roots are taken from any message content, including tool results that carry untrusted text (fetched pages, the PR's own files and diff), and absolute paths are accepted unchanged. findReviewGateState then folds closedAt from every root into one value and returns null (gate released) when any root holds a review-flow package closed since session start that is newer than the chosen package's manifest. Attack vector: a PR adds `docs/.metaproject/reviews/x/manifest.json` with mode review-flow and status closed and mentions that path in its text; when the PR head is checked out after the round's manifest was last written, the file's mtime is >= since, the agent reads the path into history, and the gate releases while the real package is still open. Separately, an open package another concurrent session opened in a named sibling worktree can be chosen as `best` when cwd has no active pointer, holding this session on the wrong review.
impact: The completion gate (which keeps the model working until `keryx review complete` accepts) can be released or misdirected by content the reviewer does not control. `review complete` itself still refuses, so no false completion is recorded; the harm is an unfinished round the model stops on. Minor: hardening of a workflow gate whose bypass leaves the record honest.
suggested_fix: Harvest roots only from the agent's own tool-call arguments (not tool results), and accept an extra root only when it holds an active-review pointer written in this session or is inside the cwd's git top level. Compute closedAt only for the root (or reviewId) of the package actually chosen, so a closed package elsewhere cannot release the gate for this one.
evidence: src/review/completion-gate.ts:61-64 (content and call.arguments scanned alike), :65 (path.resolve accepts absolute prefixes), :129-136 (closedAt = max over all roots, compared with best.mtime). History passed from src/commands/agent.ts:3487 includes tool messages.
